title: Field-based Invertebrate Molecular Diagnostics Using a BentoLab
author: Jordan P Cuff
materials: Weigh 0.5 g, agarose and set it aside.
Once complete, remove the tubes from the thermocycler and move onto the next step, or refrigerate if pausing.

steps.title: Collect and kill specimens
steps.instruction: Collect invertebrates by pitfall traps (flush rim, mesh lid, 12‑24 h dry or 48‑72 h with preservative), hand searching (standardised area/time, collect with pooter or tubes), or sweep netting (fixed‑length strip, figure‑of‑eight motion). Kill live specimens by placing an ethyl‑acetate‑soaked cotton ball in the collection pot for up to 10 min, or freeze at –20 °C for at least 1 h.

steps.title: Identify specimens taxonomically
steps.instruction: Identify each collected invertebrate to at least order level using appropriate taxonomic keys or reference guides, either in the field or back in the lab.

steps.title: Isolate target tissue
steps.instruction: Using a sterilised scalpel and forceps (dip/soak in Chemgene or bleach, water, then ethanol before and after each use), excise 1‑2 mm of the desired tissue (e.g., gut contents) and place it into a 0.2 mL PCR tube.

steps.title: Prepare alkaline lysis reagent
steps.instruction: To make 25 mL alkaline lysis reagent (25 mM NaOH, 0.2 mM EDTA), add 6.25 mL 0.1 M NaOH and 10 µL 0.5 M EDTA to 24.365 mL molecular‑grade nuclease‑free water. Store at room temperature and use within 1‑2 months.

steps.title: Add alkaline lysis to samples
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL alkaline lysis reagent to each tube containing tissue. Push the tissue down with sterilised forceps, crush lightly to expose internal material, and sterilise forceps between samples. If a compatible centrifuge is available, centrifuge briefly to ensure submersion.

steps.title: Incubate lysates
steps.instruction: Incubate tubes at 95 °C for 1 h (extend to 2 h for large, chitinous specimens).

steps.title: Prepare neutralisation reagent
steps.instruction: To make 25 mL neutralisation reagent (40 mM Tris‑HCl), add 1 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl to 24 mL molecular‑grade nuclease‑free water. Store at room temperature; use within 1‑2 months.

steps.title: Neutralise lysates
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL neutralisation reagent to each heated sample, flick the tube a few times to mix, and tap the liquid back to the tube base.

steps.title: Store lysates
steps.instruction: Store the neutralised lysates at 12 °C until further processing.

steps.title: Dilute DNA extract
steps.instruction: Transfer an aliquot of the lysate to a new tube and bring the volume to 100 µL with nuclease‑free water: 1 µL lysate for large samples, 5 µL for small samples, or 10 µL for very small samples. Keep at room temperature until PCR.

steps.title: Calculate PCR master mix
steps.instruction: For a 20 µL reaction, per tube combine: 10 µL 2X hot‑start PCR master mix, 0.5 µL forward primer (10 µM, final 0.25 µM), 0.5 µL reverse primer (10 µM, final 0.25 µM), 8 µL nuclease‑free water. Multiply component volumes by the number of reactions (including at least one negative and one positive control) and then by 1.2 (or 1.1 with calibrated pipettes). Mix the combined master mix gently by flicking and inverting a single tube.

steps.title: Add master mix to PCR tubes
steps.instruction: Dispense 19 µL of the prepared master mix into each 0.2 mL PCR tube that will receive a sample (including controls). Label tubes clearly.

steps.title: Add DNA template
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL of each diluted DNA extract to its corresponding tube; add 1 µL nuclease‑free water to the negative‑control tube.

steps.title: Run thermocycler program
steps.instruction: Place tubes in the thermocycler and run: 95 °C 3:00 min (initial denaturation); 35 cycles of 95 °C 0:30 s (denaturation), annealing at primer‑specific temperature 0:30 s, 72 °C 0:30 s (extension); 72 °C 5:00 min (final extension); hold at 12 °C indefinitely.

steps.title: Prepare 2 % agarose gel
steps.instruction:
For a 25 mL gel (2 % w/v):
• Option A (microwave): weigh 25 g (≈25 mL) 1X borax solution, add agarose, microwave until bubbling, mix, repeat microwaving until solution is clear of lumps.
• Option B (no microwave): weigh 22.5 g water, bring to boil in a travel kettle, add agarose and 2.5 mL 10X borax solution, mix thoroughly until clear.
Before the gel sets, add 2 µL gel dye (e.g., SYBRSafe) and mix.

steps.title: Cast gel with combs
steps.instruction: Set the gel tray with enough combs for all samples, pour the molten agarose into the tray, and allow it to solidify for 15‑25 min.

steps.title: Add DNA dye to PCR products
steps.instruction: Add 4 µL DNA loading dye to each completed PCR tube and mix gently.

steps.title: Load gel with samples
steps.instruction:
After the gel has set, remove the combs. Submerge the gel in 1X borax buffer (wells positioned at the negative electrode). Load wells as follows:
1. Add 1 µL DNA ladder to the first well of each row.
2. Add 4 µL dyed PCR product of each sample to separate wells.
3. Ensure wells are correctly labelled.

steps.title: Run electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Run the gel at 100 V for 25 min (or, if using a full‑size tank, up to 300 V for 10‑15 min). Observe bubble formation and dye migration.

steps.title: Visualise and document gel
steps.instruction: Turn off the power, remove the gel, blot dry with tissue, place it on a transilluminator (or BentoLab gel‑doc), cover appropriately, photograph, and assess band patterns, paying special attention to positive and negative controls.

steps.title: Prepare 1 X borax buffer
steps.instruction: Dilute 2.5 mL 10X borax solution with 22.5 mL water to obtain 25 mL 1X borax buffer. If 10X borax stock is needed, dissolve 1.91 g sodium tetraborate decahydrate in 100 mL water, heat and stir until clear.
